newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Gas oil steady as buyers pause.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Gas oil steady as buyers pause.

text.p: After last week's frenzy when about 3.25 million barrels were traded, buyers in Singapore took a pause on Monday as prices remained well supported, traders said.
Bids for physical cargoes were seen earlier at steady levels of $26.80 for end April/early May barrels, and $27.20 for May 6-10 lifting fob, with three offers seen at $27.30.
But traders would not yet commit themselves into saying that a buying spree by two Singapore traders have come to an end, which explained why values remained firm.

The respite in trading activities gave the market time to digest what has happened over the past one month when the Singapore traders bought a massive 13 million barrels, which would have cost them a a whopping $350 million.

Traders were concerned that gas oil values could even drop to $23.00 a barrel if the Singapore traders suddenly withdrew from the market and leave many traders with arbitrage cargoes, most of which has been absorbed by the buyers, stranded with low-priced oil.
Sellers now feel that they are at the mercy of the local traders and are reasessing their positions.

But the continued strength of the Asian market compared with the West is continuing to open arbitrge opportunities, this time from the Caribbean, even though the recent rally in European values was fast closing the arbitrage from Europe as the current spread narrowed to around $20.00 per tonne.

The swaps market rose following last week's large purchases of the shutdown of a 27,500-barrel-per-day at the 125,000-bpd Dumai refinery followinga fire late on Friday. May gained 40 cents earlier before shaving off 20 cents from the high to be last quoted at $25.80/$25.90 a barrel.
India is expected to issue a gas oil import tender for June arrival on Tuesday, while Taiwan is also expected to float a sale tender for June lifting.
Jet fuel was quiet with no bids or offers seen, but the swaps regrade improved to minus 40/20 cents per barrel from Friday's minus 50/30 cents.
